clue.text: Prohibit return of dog put inside

parts.note: to prohibit is to ban

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word for the dog is read from its end

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: A ban on bringing a dog back into the house once it has been let out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put inside' reads as part of the dog story but is the definition: to bang up is British slang for locking someone in a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang up is informal British slang meaning to imprison or lock someone in a cell.

clue.text: Capricious piece by artist on railway after sunrise?

indicators.note: after says the whole run of earlier wordplay follows the final piece, so that last piece is written first

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god, and in a down entry a rising name reads from the bottom up
a piece is a bit
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A whimsical painting of a railway at dawn, as if a surrealist artist had chosen it on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunrise' splits into the sun god and the instruction to rise; in a down clue that sends the god upward. The words after 'piece' are placed after it in the order given.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbitrary choices follow whim rather than reason, which is what capricious behaviour means.

clue.text: Land of 21 6s

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a country of West Africa
second meaning: 6 is the entry SHILLING, and twenty-one shillings made the old coin of this name

explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle is themed on old British money; '6s' means several of the answer to 6 down, the shilling, the coin of 12 old pence.
explanation.definitionFit: The West African republic shares its name with the old gold coin worth one pound and one shilling.

clue.text: Tiresome way to get over the wall when confined outside

indicators.note: the word for confined is placed outside, wrapping around the way over the wall

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut in

parts.words: way to get over the wall
parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a wall or fence

explanation.surface: A tedious business, trying to escape over a prison wall while locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: A stile is the step built into a British field wall or fence so walkers can cross it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilent literally means plague-carrying, and is used loosely of anything annoying or troublesome.

clue.text: Split a trifle with dry inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the word for dry goes into the word for a trifle

parts.note: a trifle is a small amount, a bit
sec is French for dry, used of wine

explanation.surface: Cutting a trifle pudding in two, with a dry sherry soaked inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is a British layered pudding of sponge, custard and cream, often laced with sherry; here it just means a little bit.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two equal parts, so it is a precise way to split.

clue.text: Sir Toby to be left at church

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Sir Toby, perhaps a Victorian squire, is to be dropped off at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' simply places the church after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Toby Belch is the drunken uncle of Olivia in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.

clue.text: All those cut off have badly inserted in bone with string

indicators.note: inserted in places the first word inside the bone word

parts.note: the shin bone is the tibia
ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated
the G string is a violin string

explanation.surface: Everyone amputated has had a bone badly patched with string.
explanation.walkthrough: To be cut off with a shilling was to be disinherited, left a token sum in a will. A shilling was the old British coin worth twelve pence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'cut off with a shilling' describes heirs left only a token coin, so everyone so treated has one.

clue.text: 5 6s per head?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: five shillings, the old coin worth a quarter of a pound
second meaning: the top of the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Per head' looks like a price for each person, but the two words split; the crown was an old British coin worth five shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: The coin was worth five shillings, and the same word names the top of the skull.

clue.text: Retroactive virus disposes of gadget

indicators.note: retro means backwards, so the virus word is read in the other direction

parts.note: a bug is an informal word for a virus
to bin something is to throw it away

explanation.surface: A retrovirus attacks and destroys some device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retroactive virus' plays on retrovirus, a real kind of virus.
explanation.definitionFit: Gubbins is informal British for a gadget or bits of apparatus whose name escapes you.

clue.text: Undercoats should be disregarded

parts.note: surface reading: a painter's instruction that primer layers need a topcoat of shiny paint on them
setter's reading: the phrase for something passed over quickly and ignored

explanation.walkthrough: The decorator's sense, an undercoat covered with gloss paint, and the figurative sense, something skated over, share one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To gloss over a matter is to treat it superficially and pay it no proper attention.

clue.text: Stunned and prepared for burial

definitions.meaning: first meaning: knocked flat by a blow
second meaning: a corpse arranged for viewing before a funeral

explanation.surface: A boxer knocked out so cold he might as well be ready for the undertaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means knocked unconscious, and also describes a dead body washed and arranged before the funeral.

clue.text: Internationals prove suitable partners

parts.note: to prove something is to test it
a good match is a well-suited partner

explanation.surface: Dating advice: finding out whether two people make a suitable couple.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket or rugby game.
explanation.definitionFit: Test matches are the full international fixtures between national teams, especially in cricket.

clue.text: Proceeding more or less OK, being correctly pointed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: going about something in a broadly sound way
second meaning: a train whose points are set properly runs along the proper track

explanation.walkthrough: Railway points are the movable rails that switch a train from one track to another, so a correctly pointed train is literally on proper rails.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means approaching a problem in roughly the correct way, and literally describes a train set onto the proper track.

clue.text: Outstanding actors' horoscope
Cat that sounds like a little bird: I see, but I shouldn't

parts.words: that sounds like a little bird
parts.note: a chick's high cry is a peep, so something making that noise is doing as a little bird does
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A tomcat chirping like a fledgling, and a confession of seeing what one shouldn't.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat comes first in the clue but last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyeur spies on others secretly, so the first-person confession of looking where one should not describes him.

clue.text: Rail's way forward includes hair on a pole

definitions.note: the permanent way is the track bed of a railway; the answer is the first word of that phrase

indicators.note: includes means the word for forward holds the rest inside it

parts.note: a forward person is cheeky, pert
a mane is a long growth of hair
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Progress on the railway seems to involve a horse's mane on a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way forward' looks like one phrase but splits: 'way' finishes the definition and 'forward' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway engineers call the finished track the permanent way, as opposed to temporary construction lines.

clue.text: Rail journey: if wet, by river in flow

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the word for flow

parts.note: the tide is the flow of the sea
wet weather is rain
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A train trip in the rain alongside a flowing river.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling by train is a trip along the rails, which is what a rail journey is.

clue.text: …of such a remote object comes to 21

definitions.note: read with the clue number: sixteen of these coins come to the answer at 21, the groat

parts.note: remote means distant, far
an object is a thing

explanation.surface: Something so distant that it seems to arrive from far away.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis tells you to begin with the clue's own number, 16. A farthing was a quarter of an old penny and a groat four pence, so sixteen farthings made a groat.
explanation.definitionFit: Four farthings made a penny and a groat was fourpence, so sixteen farthings exactly equal one groat.

clue.text: Portable power source for teetotal assault

parts.note: a dry person drinks no alcohol
battery is the legal term for a physical assault

explanation.surface: A power source for a temperance campaigner's attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry cell uses a paste electrolyte rather than liquid, so it can be carried around to supply electricity.

clue.text: See 12
2 6s for keeping student at home

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
L is a learner driver, the crossword student
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Paying a couple of shillings to have a student lodge at home.
explanation.walkthrough: A florin was the old British two-shilling coin, worth a tenth of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The florin coin was worth exactly two shillings in British money before decimalisation.

clue.text: Nuts? Raving: then a clue is needed

indicators.note: needed sounds like kneaded, and kneaded dough is worked into a new shape

parts.note: every letter of these words

explanation.surface: A frantic solver, driven mad, demands another hint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts?' looks like a cry that someone is mad, but it is a meal of nuts, with the question mark flagging the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatless midday meal could well consist of nuts, so nuts are an example of one.

clue.text: One of John's is 3rd of 6

definitions.meaning: first meaning: John o' ..., the village at the northern tip of mainland Scotland
second meaning: a coin worth four pence, a third of a shilling

explanation.walkthrough: John o' Groats is the far north-eastern village of mainland Britain; a groat was an old fourpenny coin, and a shilling (6 down) was twelve pence.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourpenny coin was a third of a twelve-penny shilling, and the place name contains its plural.

clue.text: Dance that is sweet when the last part's repeated

parts.words: that is sweet when the last part's repeated
parts.note: a rum baba is a sponge pudding soaked in rum syrup, whose last syllable comes twice

explanation.surface: A dance that becomes a pudding once its ending is said again.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the dance with its final two letters doubled is the dessert, so the dessert minus one repeat is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance in four-four time.

clue.text: Silvery metal carrier, one with peculiar surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings are what lies all around, so the word for peculiar wraps the other pieces

parts.note: rum is British informal for odd or peculiar
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A shiny metal vessel stands in strange surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surroundings' completes the container signal begun by 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodium is a rare, hard, silver-white element of the platinum group.

clue.text: First potatoes? You shouldn't believe what you hear!

wordplay.words: You shouldn't believe what you hear!
wordplay.note: the organ you hear with is not telling the truth

explanation.surface: A warning against trusting gossip, beside a gardener's question about new potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Earlies are the first potatoes of the season. The second half is a cryptic way of saying the listening organ tells untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners call the season's first-cropping potato varieties earlies, as distinct from maincrop varieties.

clue.text: Where blame and pollen are attached

definitions.text: Where blame and pollen are attached

parts.note: surface reading: a mark of disgrace that clings to someone
setter's reading: the part of a flower's pistil that catches pollen grains

explanation.walkthrough: One word serves both: the disgrace that attaches to someone, and the sticky tip of a flower's female organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A social mark of shame clings to a person, and in botany the receptive tip of the pistil is where pollen sticks.

clue.text: Leather worker, half of 6

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who cures hides into leather
second meaning: slang for a sixpence, half a shilling

explanation.walkthrough: 6 is the answer at 6 down, the shilling; a tanner was British slang for the sixpenny coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman cures animal skins with tannin, and old slang named the sixpenny coin, worth half a shilling, the same.
